question.text: Sodium extract is heated with concentrated <math><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> before testing for halogens because :

options.text: <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></math>  and AgCN are soluble in acidic medium.
Silver halides are totally insoluble in nitric acid.

<math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> , if present, are decomposed by conc. <math><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> and hence do not interfere in the test.
Ag reacts faster with halides in acidic medium

solution.text: <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> ions if present are decomposed by conc. <math><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> and hence do not interfere in the test.
